concerns.text: FR-010/Step 3: Calculating Pearson correlation between 'Generalization Gap slope' and 'HumanEval score' is methodologically invalid for N=1 per model. The plan trains one AR and one MDM model. You cannot calculate a correlation coefficient (r) between two variables (gap slope, HumanEval score) when you only have two data points (one pair for AR, one pair for MDM). A correlation requires a distribution of samples (N > 2) to be statistically meaningful. This analysis is mathematically undefined for the proposed experimental design.

Power Analysis: The plan treats 'Epochs' (100) as the sample size (N) for a repeated-measures ANOVA to detect an interaction between Model Type and Epoch. This is a category error. In a repeated-measures design comparing two groups (AR vs MDM), the degrees of freedom for the interaction depend on the number of subjects (models), not the number of time points. With N=2 models, the interaction term has 1 degree of freedom, and the error term is derived from the variance between these two specific models. You cannot achieve statistical power (0.8) to detect an interaction effect with only two independent experimental units (the two models), regardless of how many epochs are measured. The 'sample size' is 2, not 100.

FR-005: Repeated-Measures ANOVA on Generalization Gap (Model × Epoch) is invalid with N=2 groups. ANOVA assumes independence of observations and sufficient degrees of freedom to estimate error variance. With only two models (one AR, one MDM), there is no within-group variance to estimate. The 'interaction' will be a deterministic difference between two curves, not a statistical inference. The p-value will be meaningless or undefined. The analysis plan must be revised to use a different metric (e.g., area under the gap curve) or a different experimental design (training multiple seeds of each architecture) to generate a valid statistical test.
